root_idea.summary: The root's clearest orientation is movement through the night—travel or passage from one point to another—with extensions to movement beneath a surface and to transmission or spread.
root_idea.development: The verbal branch distinguishes nocturnal travel from causing or leading someone to travel by night. Related nouns name night journeys, travelers, and groups that travel at night; figurative usage describes something creeping, spreading, or extending through another thing. The stream sense reflects something that runs or passes along.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic imperfect is presented under the normalized Form I perfect citation form سَرَى.
The Quranic imperative and perfect forms are presented under the normalized Form IV citation form أَسْرَىٰ.
The Quranic nominal is presented under the citation form سَرِيّ.

senses.definition: To travel or journey by night.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive nocturnal-travel use. The Quranic form is imperfect; the dictionary headword is the perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To pass away or go on, of the night.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the Quranic expression concerning the night as it goes away. Some interpreters understand the expression instead as referring to traveling in the night; that reading belongs to the night-travel sense.

senses.definition: To cause or lead someone to travel by night; to transport by night.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ for the person or group accompanying or being transported. In the Quran it describes leading a group forth by night and transporting a servant by night.
The Quranic term in the account of Mary; the lexical evidence includes a rivulet running toward palm trees as a possible specification.

senses.definition: Elevated or noble; an alternative interpretation of the Quranic term.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative reading of the expression in 19:24 connects the term with elevation or nobility rather than with a stream.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To creep or extend beneath the ground, said of the root of a tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete extension of movement along an unseen path.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spread, pass into, or extend through something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of poison, wine, calamity, war, anxiety, the effects of a wound, legal prohibition, or emancipation; anxiety may thereby come upon someone or pass away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To load goods, utensils, or furniture onto the back of a beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use distinct from nocturnal travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove or pull off a garment from someone or from its place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may be transitive or describe a garment being removed; the intensified form is also reported in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send a military detachment against an enemy by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an army leader dispatching a سَرِيَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exude sweat from the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II bodily-process use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Night journeying or a night journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Related nominal forms include سَرْيَةٌ for a single night journey and سِرَايَةٌ for the act or state of traveling by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small, short, round, smooth arrowhead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal form associated with سِرْوَةٌ; the source distinguishes it from the doubled form used for a military detachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A locust in its larval first state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal variant of the term for the early-stage locust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain tree whose fine wood is used for making bows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of unity is also reported for the tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A detached portion or company of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is conventionally associated with a group selected from an army and historically applied to groups of varying size; it was originally connected with marching by night but was also used of groups marching by day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pervasive or spreading throughout.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term reported in philosophical writings and identified as probably post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Syriac language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A language name formed from the related pervasive or spreading terminology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who travels much or often by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun emphasizing habitual or frequent nocturnal travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person traveling by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial noun for a nocturnal traveler.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation attributed to the lion's going about by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A party or company of people traveling by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from the military term سَرِيَّةٌ, though both can denote a group associated with nocturnal movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud or rain cloud that comes or travels by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to a night cloud, a night rain, or a cloud situated between early-morning and evening clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Donkeys or wild asses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural usage explained by their resting little or grazing by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A column or pillar; also a mast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A structural vertical support, including a stone or baked-brick column and a ship's mast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most accustomed to traveling by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective, distinct from the Form IV verb أَسْرَىٰ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or time of night travel; also a way or route.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may function as a noun of place, time, or action and may be used more broadly for a way by which one goes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who goes forth in or among a سَرِيَّة, a detached company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun derived from the military-detachment sense.

cautions: The Quranic سَرِيًّا in 19:24 has two reported interpretations in the supplied evidence: a stream or rivulet, and an alternative connection with elevation or nobility.

Some discussions offer an alternative derivation of أَسْرَىٰ from سَرَاةٌ or the related root associated with elevation or a wide tract. The displayed Form IV sense follows the direct Quranic night-transport evidence.
The Mufradat discussion of ﴿وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَاعَةً﴾ in يوسف 12:19 concerns the form أَسَرُّوهُ from a different root and is not assigned to this root's Quranic forms.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Mufradat row includes the expression ﴿وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَاعَةً﴾ [يوسف 12:19], but its consonantal root is س ر ر rather than the canonical QAC root س ر ي; it is therefore excluded from the form senses.

The alternative elevation-based interpretation of سَرِيًّا is reported through a connection with السرو and is represented as an alternative Quranic interpretation rather than as an uncontested independent root meaning.
